```markdown
# SEC filing ingestion — Roadmap

> For agentic workers: REQUIRED SKILL: derive-roadmap — resume via its
> reconcile step; route each unticked stage per its ROUTING line; never plan
> this document wholesale.

## Outcomes

Source: your partner's words, 2026-11-06. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md, specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 uv workspace with four package scaffolds (repo state at the initial commit).
Choices made: deployment platform not chosen; the Azure ADR is Proposed and is background only.

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | The quarterly and daily index files, ingested into one filing-index table | A | 1 | Small: about 130 quarterly files since 1993 plus one daily file per business day, minutes of downloading at 3 requests/second (SEC full-index and daily-index directories); measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | The individual submissions that the index rows name, downloaded | A | 2 | Large: millions of files, weeks for the full history at 3 requests/second (index row count × request rate; not yet measured); per-file cost measured by Stage 2 |
| O3 | 10-K and 8-K filings picked out of the submissions, with their main documents extracted | A | 3 | Unknown until submissions are on disk; measured by Stage 3 |

Tracks: A — SEC filing ingestion (known progression: index files, then submissions, then 10-K and 8-K handling, then hardening).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Index files core
      Objective: Load one archived quarter's master index and the daily indexes that follow it from real SEC data into one filing-index table.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing (package scaffolds only)
      Produces: a queryable filing-index table for the loaded range; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: the table holds every row of the loaded quarterly and daily files, no filing appears twice where the files overlap, and the findings file records bytes downloaded, rows loaded, request count and elapsed time of the real run.
      Leaves out: shared request budget across concurrent collectors → Stage 4; manifests, generations, active pointer and replay from raw → Stage 5; full-history backfill and daily catch-up → Stage 6; reconciliation and withdrawals → Stage 7; scheduling and deployment → Stage 10
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Submissions core
      Objective: Download the submissions named by a bounded slice of Stage 1's table from real SEC data.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 1's filing-index table
      Produces: the downloaded submissions for that slice, located by their index rows; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-2-findings.md
      Exit: every index row in the slice maps to a downloaded submission or a recorded failure, and the findings file records files, bytes, requests and elapsed time per file, with the full-history time extrapolated from them.
      Leaves out: resumable, budget-shared collection → Stage 4; full-history download → Stage 8; deployment → Stage 10
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: 10-K and 8-K core
      Objective: Pick the 10-K and 8-K filings out of Stage 2's submissions and extract their main documents.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 2's downloaded submissions
      Produces: extracted main documents for the slice's 10-K and 8-K filings; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-3-findings.md
      Exit: each 10-K and 8-K in the slice has its main document extracted or a recorded reason it could not be, and the findings file records counts and elapsed time of the real run.
      Leaves out: historical format coverage across the full range → Stage 9; deployment → Stage 10
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Shared SEC access and resumable collection
      Objective: Route every SEC request through one downloader and one request budget, with per-file checkpoints and retained original bytes (background spec §4.3, R6, R8).
      Outcomes: O1, O2
      Consumes: Stages 1–2 collectors
      Produces: one downloader that index and submission collection both use; resumable collection
      Exit: index and submission collectors running together stay within the one configured request rate, and an interrupted run resumes without re-downloading completed files.
      Leaves out: deployment-wide coordination → Stage 10
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Versioned index catalog
      Objective: Publish the filing-index table as versioned generations with manifests and one active pointer, rebuilt from retained raw files (background spec §4.4 identity, §4.5, §4.6).
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stage 1's table; Stage 4's retained raw files
      Produces: a filing-index catalog that readers resolve through the active pointer
      Exit: a parser-version change rebuilds the catalog from raw storage with no SEC requests and no duplicate filings, and a crash before the pointer update leaves the prior generation readable.
      Leaves out: reconciliation and withdrawals → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Full index backfill and daily catch-up
      Objective: Backfill the index over the full chosen history and catch daily ingestion up across missed runs and quarter boundaries (background spec §4.2).
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stages 4–5
      Produces: the filing-index catalog over the full chosen range, with a gap report
      Exit: every requested quarter is published or listed as a gap in the run report, and a run after a multi-quarter outage catches up without losing pending older files.
      Leaves out: scheduled operation → Stage 10
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Index reconciliation and withdrawals
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes and apply additions and changes, gating closed-quarter withdrawals on approval (background spec §4.4, R7, R10).
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stages 5–6
      Produces: a reconciled catalog with recorded changes
      Exit: a changed quarterly file publishes its additions and updates, and a replacement that removes filings stays unpublished until an approval naming its hash is recorded.
      Leaves out: scheduled reconciliation → Stage 10
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Full submissions download
      Objective: Download the submissions for the full chosen range through Stage 4's downloader.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 4; Stage 6's catalog; Stage 2's findings
      Produces: submissions on disk for the full chosen range
      Exit: every index row in the range maps to a downloaded submission or a reported failure, and the run report records total files, bytes and elapsed time.
      Leaves out: scheduled incremental download → Stage 10
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 9: 10-K and 8-K at full scale
      Objective: Extract main documents for every 10-K and 8-K in Stage 8's submissions, covering the historical formats in range.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 3; Stage 8
      Produces: extracted main documents for all 10-K and 8-K filings in range
      Exit: each 10-K and 8-K in range has an extracted main document or a reported reason, and committed fixtures cover every format found in range.
      Leaves out: scheduled extraction → Stage 10
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 10: Deployment, scheduling and monitoring
      Objective: Run daily ingestion, reconciliation, submission download and extraction on a schedule on the chosen platform, with alerts and runbooks (background ADR; background spec §4.1, §4.7–§4.9).
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3
      Consumes: Stages 4–9
      Produces: scheduled operation
      Exit: observed scheduled runs complete with durable reports, and a failed run raises an alert.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, which writing-plans copies verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-ingestion-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, run derive-roadmap §6 over the Outcomes list: each of O1–O3 gets a verdict with evidence (implementing stage and plan, Deviation notes, deferred_items entries). An unmet outcome becomes a new stage or a written deferral before the roadmap retires to `specs/completed/`.
```
